description: Creates a new patient demographic record. Optionally creates an associated primary contact (patient_contacts) when contact/email is supplied.

body.gender: string(30), required at API layer (nullable at DB layer)
body.dateOfBirth: date, required at API layer (nullable at DB layer)
body.title: string(20), optional
body.contact: string, optional - convenience field, inserted into patient_contacts as contact_type = PHONE
body.email: string, optional - convenience field, inserted into patient_contacts as contact_type = EMAIL

validation: firstName must not be null (NOT NULL at DB layer)
gender and dateOfBirth are nullable at the DB layer but required at the API layer per documented contract
dateOfBirth must be a valid date
if contact/email provided, resulting patient_contacts row must be unique per (organization_id, branch_id, contact_type, contact_value) -- uq_patient_contact

errors.condition: firstName missing/null, or gender/dateOfBirth missing (API-layer required)
dateOfBirth is not a valid date / gender or patientType is not a recognized value
Duplicate patient contact (same contact_type + contact_value already exists in organization + branch)
organizationId or branchId does not exist

constraints: patients.gender, date_of_birth are NULLABLE at DB layer

notes: SCHEMA GAP: database/api_contracts_test/010_patient_management.sql inserts into a patients.patient_code column and tests 'Duplicate Patient Code' (API-T065) as a 409 scenario, but no patient_code column exists on the patients table in any schema file, including the current database/schema/versions/v25.sql snapshot - the test script would fail with 'column does not exist' if run against the live schema. There is also no other DB-level uniqueness constraint on the patients table itself (no unique index on name/DOB), so the 'Prevent Duplicate Patient Record' rule (PM005 in the Functionality Tracker, noted there as 'Depends on business rules') is NOT currently enforced by the database - the only real per-tenant uniqueness in this area is uq_patient_identifier on the separate patient_identifiers table (organization_id, branch_id, identifier_type, identifier_value), which is a distinct, not-yet-contracted functionality (PM006-010 in the tracker).
requires_confirmation: Is patient_code a planned column that has not yet been migrated into the schema, or should duplicate-patient detection be implemented via patient_identifiers (e.g. an MRN identifier_type) instead? The Functionality Tracker explicitly defers this decision ('Depends on business rules') and no schema migration currently backs it.
